root_cause.text: AppArmor’s policy namespace creation in `__aa_create_ns()` lacked any maximum nesting-depth check, because it incorrectly relied on user-namespace limits even though `struct aa_ns` hierarchies are not strictly tied to user namespaces and can be nested arbitrarily deep.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the number of policy namespaces is not bounded relying on the user namespace limit” and that they “aren't strictly tied to user namespaces,” allowing arbitrary deep nesting for resource exhaustion; the patch adds `#define MAX_NS_DEPTH 32` and rejects creation in `__aa_create_ns()` with `if (parent->level > MAX_NS_DEPTH) return ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC);`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states “the number of policy namespaces is not bounded relying on the user namespace limit” and that they “aren't strictly tied to user namespaces,” allowing arbitrary deep nesting for resource exhaustion; the patch adds `#define MAX_NS_DEPTH 32` and rejects creation in `__aa_create_ns()` with `if (parent->level > MAX_NS_DEPTH) return ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a named maximum namespace depth constant set to 32 to align with the user namespace depth limit.
intent_record.what: A new comment and preprocessor macro definition were added near the top of the file: `/* Match max depth of user namespaces */` and `#define MAX_NS_DEPTH 32`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant representing the maximum namespace depth of 32, allowing subsequent code in the file to use a shared limit aligned with user namespace depth instead of a hardcoded value; by itself, this hunk does not change runtime behavior until the constant is referenced elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a maximum namespace depth check in __aa_create_ns() to reject over-deep namespace creation with -ENOSPC before allocation.
intent_record.what: An early conditional check was added in __aa_create_ns() to test whether parent->level is greater than MAX_NS_DEPTH, and if so the function now immediately returns ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC) before calling alloc_ns().
intent_record.how: This prevents creation of a new namespace when the parent namespace depth already exceeds the allowed maximum, avoiding allocation and propagation of an invalid deeper namespace hierarchy and instead reporting the condition as an ENOSPC error.

grouping_result.intent: Add a named maximum namespace depth constant set to 32 to align with the user namespace depth limit.
Add a maximum namespace depth check in __aa_create_ns() to reject over-deep namespace creation with -ENOSPC before allocation.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is caused by missing maximum nesting-depth enforcement for AppArmor policy namespaces. Adding a named maximum namespace depth constant directly introduces the limit needed to address that root cause.
The change directly fixes the root cause by adding the missing maximum nesting-depth check in __aa_create_ns(), preventing arbitrarily deep AppArmor policy namespace hierarchies.

candidates.rationale: Namespace creation proceeds directly to allocation without any prior maximum nesting-depth validation, embodying the missing check that allowed arbitrarily deep AppArmor namespace hierarchies.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement shows __aa_create_ns() proceeding directly to namespace allocation without first enforcing any maximum AppArmor namespace nesting-depth limit. That missing precondition enabled creation of arbitrarily deep aa_ns hierarchies, matching the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code is sufficient because it includes the namespace creation path in this commit: `__aa_create_ns(...)`, `__aa_find_or_create_ns(...)`, and `aa_prepare_ns(...)`. The root cause is the absence of any maximum nesting-depth check when creating AppArmor namespaces. In `__aa_create_ns(struct aa_ns *parent, const char *name, struct dentry *dir)`, the function allocates and links a new namespace with `ns = alloc_ns(parent->base.hname, name);`, creates the fs entry with `error = __aa_fs_ns_mkdir(ns, ns_subns_dir(parent), name);`, sets `ns->parent = aa_get_ns(parent);`, and adds it via `list_add_rcu(&ns->base.list, &parent->sub_ns);`. There is no check on parent depth, no comparison against any max nesting constant, and no rejection of excessively deep hierarchies. Likewise, `__aa_find_or_create_ns(...)` and `aa_prepare_ns(...)` only check for existence and otherwise call `__aa_create_ns(parent, name, ...)`; they do not enforce any namespace nesting limit. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present in this commit.

New namespaces are created when lookup fails: `ns = alloc_namespace(root->base.hname, name);` and then linked as a child with `ns->parent = aa_get_namespace(root);` and `list_add_rcu(&ns->base.list, &root->sub_ns);`. There is no check anywhere in this function, nor in `alloc_namespace()`, for a maximum AppArmor namespace nesting depth before creating a child namespace. The root cause states that `__aa_create_ns()` was vulnerable because it lacked any maximum nesting-depth check for `struct aa_ns` hierarchies; this commit's namespace creation path likewise allows arbitrary child creation under the current namespace with no depth validation.
